conflicts.description: Printed p. 27 draws lamp 36 in both the backbox inset and the upper-left playfield. Its list and printed p. 49 identify a backbox lamp. The retained VPX uses lamp 36 for a playfield red cover and glow. The documented backbox lamp is retained. Fitment and quantity of any playfield sockets on this circuit remain unresolved. Resolution path: have an owner or restorer run the discrete lamp 36 test and trace the circuit at both the backbox and the lower end of the upper-left Transporter assembly.

drivers.variant_notes: CPU 1.17 and display 1.09 are the matched factory update in Service Bulletin 31. It addresses tech alerts, ball launch and display synchronization, and adds a restart-game adjustment.

inputs.label: Unused Flipper Column Lower Right End-of-Stroke (81)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPEOSBIT = 0x01, published at 81 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. locals.flipMask carries this end-of-stroke bit only when hw.flippers sets FLIP_EOS (implied by FLIP_SOL), and FLIP1516 = FLIP_SWNO(15,16) sets neither, so core_updateSw neither synthesizes it nor copies it anywhere: PinMAME models no end-of-stroke switch on this machine. A host write survives in the column, but the ROM cannot read it there: s11.c's pia4a_r reads the switch matrix only through core_getSwCol with an eight-bit column strobe, which reaches columns 1-8.

inputs.label: Lower Right Flipper Button (PinMAME Flipper Column)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPBUTBIT = 0x02, published at 82 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. This is the lower right cabinet flipper button as the ROM receives it. The driver declares FLIP1516 = FLIP_SWNO(15,16) with no FLIP_SOL, so with keyboard handling off (the LibPinMAME default) core_updateSw reads this bit as the host wrote it and, on every update, copies it into matrix switch 16 through core_setSw and fabricates the synthetic 45/46 flipper outputs from it while the switched-solenoid enable is on. Drive this address, not 16: a host write to 16 is overwritten on the next update. The factory cabinet wiring diagram shows the normally open right button.

The factory jumper table specifies J8 installed. This grounds PIA 11B PA7 against its RA19-9 pull-up. PinMAME supplies PA7 from DIP bank 0 bit 0, with the fresh-state default 0 corresponding to installed and 1 to removed. All seven checked CPUs configure PA as output on boot and during periodic initialization. The two reviewed reads acknowledge an interrupt or blink PA4 in the fatal loop. Both 2.01 switch-test runs gave the same readings with host values 0 and 1. The alternate physical jumper position has no documented operator function.

mechanisms.behavior: The drain places a ball on 10. Outhole coil 1 lifts it into the gravity-fed trough. The three switches sense individual ball positions. Coil 2 ejects the ball at the shooter end. A jam can leave the outhole or release-end switch active while the ROM retries.
mechanisms.label: Three-Ball Trough and Outhole

mechanisms.behavior: The trough serves the shooter lane. A ball closes 14 in that lane. The cabinet launch command on 30 fires coil 3 in the 2.01 start probe.
mechanisms.label: Turbo Launch

mechanisms.behavior: Raise and lower drives act on a two-position ramp. Only the raised position closes switch 39. The lowered position feeds the ramp shot, and the raised position exposes the entry under it to the subway. SB32 traces intermittent failure to return down to the Ramp Up switch or a loose bobbin screw on the latch.
mechanisms.label: Transporter Up/Down Ramp

mechanisms.behavior: A switched coil lifts the gate when energized. The manual identifies a gate-lift plate assembly and the retained script opens s22 only during output 22.
mechanisms.label: Upper Ramp Gate Lift

mechanisms.behavior: A relay-driven motor turns the drive cam and stud to swing the target over the center hole. Stern's later CSI manual lists motor 515-5534-00 at 22½ RPM. Switch 25 signals a target hit. Switch 29 detects a ball in the hole. The table steps hit geometry to approximate the swing.
mechanisms.label: Swinging Target

mechanisms.behavior: The single powered cam moves a striped sliding grid across the interleaved crew and empty-room artwork. SB33 gives approximately 0.040 inch of total grid travel. Two springs bias the grid and top and bottom guides constrain its travel. The visible and hidden limits close 31 and 32 about half a cam turn apart. Only one limit may close at a time. The backbox motor runs independently of the playfield ramp and VUK. The Data East schematic shows 515-5532-00-14 on a 28 VAC feed. Stern's later CSI manual lists 500-5421-00 at 24 VAC and 3½ RPM in the Star Trek Transporter F/X row. The speed of 515-5532-00-14 remains unverified.
mechanisms.label: Backbox Transporter F/X

mechanisms.behavior: The left and center holes feed under-playfield chutes leading to the right VUK. Switch 40 senses a ball waiting in the VUK, and coil 14 ejects it. Upper-left switches 52 and 28 represent separate portions of the path.
mechanisms.label: Under-Playfield Chutes and Right VUK

mechanisms.behavior: The left outlane switch reports the ball and the laser-kick assembly can return it up the outlane when the ROM enables the feature.
mechanisms.label: Left Outlane Laser Kick

mechanisms.behavior: Four independent target contacts report dropped targets. The single reset coil raises the entire bank. Switches 20–23 run bottom to top.
mechanisms.label: Left Four-Bank Drop Targets

mechanisms.behavior: Four independent target contacts report dropped targets. The single reset coil raises the entire bank. Switches 44–47 run top to bottom.
mechanisms.label: Right Four-Bank Drop Targets

mechanisms.behavior: Cabinet switch and solid-state flipper board run one flipper assembly when enabled. Use the primary synthetic PinMAME channel for the modeled stroke.
mechanisms.label: Left Flipper
